title: Flakes of Light
subtitle: She thrusts forward, dazzling and direct.

items.text: The Long Night Singing Its Dirges
Flakes of Light
Monastery
Within the monastery, a crowd eagerly gathered on both sides of the wide-open courtyard gate.
At the forefront there stood a man, shifting in place as if anticipating something.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: Uhhem!
As if catching sight of something, he coughed into his throat and walked forward to greet the new arrival.
His demeanor shifted quickly to something more flattering.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: Lady Dikke, we're sincerely delighted to have you—
The young magistrate, striding through the door, waved her hand brusquely, as if to cut the welcome short.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: You know why I've come; your pleasantries won't impact my assessment of the work here.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: So save your proclamations of piety and duty for your flock.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: They may be more inclined to play these tedious games with you than I.
The man managed an awkward, pleading smile.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: Thank you for your... suggestion.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: The necessary records have already been organized; please follow me.
Dikke seemed uninterested in following, her gaze wandering between the passing worshipers and the flickering candles.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: Lady Dikke...?
The proud bishop raised his head, seeming quite satisfied with the lively scene inside the monastery.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: As you can see, there are many who still place their trust in us. They come to pray here each day...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Hmm...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: She chuckled briefly.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: Do you doubt the sincerity of our faith or our convictions?

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: I swear to you, My Lady; I would never bring dishonor upon our Lord...
The bishop raised his hand, deftly gesturing in front of his chest.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Rest assured; I'm not interested in your oaths either, sir.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Tell me, where might I find a tavern around here?

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: Oh, Ah?
His stance shifted, he stood his ground and spoke up.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: My Lady, surely it would be improper to be seen drinking during work hours!
Noticing nary a change in her expression, he continued cautiously.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: Moreover, the only tavern to be found here is a haven for vice... it is home only to drunkards, mud-raked and covered with lice…

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: It would be unseemly of you to be seen there.
At last, the bishop seemed to catch on, flashing a knowing smile.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: Ah, but if you're in the mood for some good wine... I happen to have some...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: You misunderstood me, Bishop Michael.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: I want only a straightforward answer.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: You failed to detail this in your records.
He smirked, laughing under his breath.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: So then this a request from the court, or...?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: It is a personal request.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: I see...
He finally eased up. The bishop stood tall, reclaiming his usual air of arrogance.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: No wonder you've become the youngest chief magistrate.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: You are not worried about upsetting the others?

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: I've heard plenty of rumors about you.
The bishop feigned a look of paternal concern. To his dismay, he couldn't detect even a hint of hesitation in the young woman.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: That's something they'll need to consider.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: No one is irreplaceable, Bishop Michael... myself included.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: The great plague claimed many lives. But we did little during that catastrophe, didn't we?

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: It wasn't our fault... there was nothing we could do...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Yet doing something is better than nothing.
The daylight was blinding, yet she stubbornly raised her head into the sun, holding it above him with authority.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: I don't intend to vex you, Bishop Michael—

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Only that I feel the sun must spread its warmth to a few more places.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Any more questions, Your Excellency?

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: No... I'll arrange for someone to guide you.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Very well.

items.speaker: Michael
items.text: May the Lord bless you.
TO BE CONTINUED…
